subject.title: PR4/5 durable core: wake controls, inspection, CLI, and Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in durable runtime, shared SQLite schema, and inspection API stack in core on the 2026.7.1 release line?
rationale: The change establishes new persistent storage, runtime ownership, environment, Gateway protocol, CLI, generated-client, and plugin SDK contracts; tests can validate implementation mechanics but cannot decide whether this architecture and release scope are intended product direction.

options.title: Sponsor inspection-first stack
options.body: Accept the core direction after enabled-runtime and upgrade proof, while retaining read-only public inspection and deferring mutation controls.

options.title: Defer beyond 2026.7.1
options.body: Keep the design work but move landing to a later release after broader lifecycle, rollback, and operator-UX review.

options.title: Decline the core architecture
options.body: Close the stack and retain only narrower independently justified reliability fixes that fit existing runtime owners.

recommendation.title: Sponsor inspection-first stack
recommendation.body: Accept the core direction after enabled-runtime and upgrade proof, while retaining read-only public inspection and deferring mutation controls.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans core architecture, persistent data, Gateway API, plugin SDK compatibility, and release ownership rather than one isolated implementation area.
